md_description: This workflow tracks donor-derived induced pluripotent stem cell lines through different culture conditions and successive passages, then measures genomic integrity using SNP arrays and whole-genome sequencing. It links physical culture manipulations, repeated genomic data acquisition, and computational variant/aberration calling to phenotype observations and integrated analysis. The resulting dataset supports evaluation of how media supplements, oxygen tension, and passaging technique affect genetic stability and helps identify culture conditions that best preserve iPSC genomic integrity.

donor_derived_ipsc_lines.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin metadata for the donor-derived iPSC starting material and excluded any culture, passage, assay, signal, or analysis fields, which belong downstream. Because this node is the root biological material, the appropriate fields are donor/sample identifiers and donor-context descriptors that explain what the lines are, not what was done to them. I avoided duplicating downstream culture-condition, passage, genomic assay, phenotype, or derived-aberration terms. I also avoided any fields already generated by implication in other nodes, especially experiment- or sample-level identifiers that should only appear once at the root. The fields below focus on provenance and donor-linked biological properties needed to interpret the iPSC lines.

md_schema.descr: Unique donor identifier for the individual from whom the iPSC line was reprogrammed; string format should match the study's donor coding scheme (for example, D001 or donor_01). Record once per starting iPSC line to link back to donor-level demographics and provenance.

Unique identifier for the established induced pluripotent stem cell line used as the starting biological material; string format should match the study's line naming convention (for example, iPSC_A03 or line_12). Record at the root entity level before any culture manipulation.

Original somatic cell type used to generate the iPSC line, recorded as the donor source cell identity before reprogramming (for example, fibroblast, peripheral_blood_mononuclear_cell, or keratinocyte).
Reported sex of the donor associated with the starting iPSC line, captured from donor records and not inferred from any downstream assay.

Donor age in years at the time the source cells were obtained for reprogramming; record as a whole number or decimal if available (typical range in this study depends on donor cohort, often 0-100+ years).

Self-reported or study-recorded donor ancestry/ethnicity category associated with the original donor. Use the study's harmonized categories when available; otherwise record the predefined cohort label used in source records.

Brief description of the source material used to generate the iPSC line, such as the original donor tissue or cell source context (for example, skin biopsy-derived fibroblasts or blood-derived cells). This captures origin only, not reprogramming protocol details.

Known baseline chromosomal status of the starting iPSC line as recorded before culture-condition experiments began, such as normal or known pre-existing abnormality. Use the study's source-line annotation rather than any later assay result.

culture_condition_setup.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the operational details of how the culture condition was applied: media supplement composition, oxygen setting, passaging technique, and other protocol parameters that define the transformation from donor-derived lines to conditioned cultures. I excluded donor identity, baseline line properties, downstream passage-specific state, genomic assay settings, raw signal/file fields, and derived aberration or phenotype outputs because those belong to upstream Entity nodes or downstream Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating any root identifiers or fields that would semantically overlap with already-generated entity metadata. The fields below are the minimum culture-protocol descriptors needed to reproduce the condition setup and interpret later stability readouts.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the applied culture-condition regimen assigned to each iPSC line during setup; use the study's condition code format (for example, CC01 or condition_A). Record at the process level to link a line to a specific culture treatment.
Basal medium used during the culture-condition setup step, recorded as the main medium formulation before supplements are added (for example, mTeSR1, E8, or DMEM/F12-based medium).

Free-text or controlled description of the media supplements added during culture setup, including any growth factors, inhibitors, serum replacements, or small molecules that define the condition. Record the exact supplement mix used at setup.

Configured oxygen concentration during culture setup, expressed as percent O2 in the incubator or chamber at the time the cells were placed into the condition. Typical values in iPSC culture are 1-21 percent.
Passaging method selected for the culture condition setup, describing how cells were dissociated and transferred during maintenance (for example, enzymatic, mechanical, or single-cell passaging).
Cell-culture substrate or feeder/support surface used during setup, recorded if the condition specifies it (for example, vitronectin, Matrigel, laminin, or feeder_layer).
Incubation temperature configured for the culture condition at setup, in degrees Celsius; typical mammalian cell-culture range is 35-39 C, with 37 C common.

Duration of the initial culture-condition exposure or equilibration period immediately after lines were placed into the defined condition, measured in hours. Use this to capture how long the setup phase lasted before downstream passage or measurement.

Brief textual note capturing any special features of the culture-condition setup not represented by the controlled fields above, such as batch-specific adjustments or rationale for the chosen regimen.

conditioned_ipsc_lines.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the cultured iPSC state after the process step, so I included intrinsic culture-state descriptors that define what the conditioned cultures are at this point: which condition they are under, how long they have been maintained, how they appear, and their general viability/status before downstream passage and assay. I excluded protocol settings from the setup process, detailed passage operations from the maintenance process, capture/instrument settings, and all raw/derived genomic or phenotype measurement outputs. I also avoided repeating donor or root-line identifiers that belong to the originating entity. The fields below help downstream users understand the state of the conditioned culture before serial passaging and measurement.

md_schema.descr: Identifier of the culture condition being carried by the iPSC culture at this entity stage; use the same study condition code assigned during setup (for example, CC01 or condition_A). This links the entity to the applied culture regimen without restating protocol parameters.

High-level state of the culture after exposure to the assigned condition and before repeated passage or measurement; indicates whether the culture is actively growing, adapted, stressed, or partially recovered.

Number of days the iPSC culture had been maintained under the assigned culture condition at this entity stage, measured from the start of the condition exposure to the time the conditioned culture record was created.

Estimated percentage of the culture surface covered by cells at the conditioned-culture observation point, typically recorded just before the next passage or downstream sampling; valid range is 0-100 percent.

Observed gross morphology of the conditioned iPSC culture before downstream processing, recorded as a qualitative culture-state descriptor such as compact colonies, differentiated areas, or heterogeneous morphology.
Estimated viable-cell fraction in the conditioned culture at the time of entity annotation, expressed as percent viable cells; typical range is 0-100 percent.
Summary indication of whether the conditioned culture retained expected iPSC-like characteristics at this stage, based on routine culture observation rather than formal downstream assay.

passage_and_maintain.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the operational parameters of routine passage and maintenance: how the cultures were split, what passage-related settings were used, how often maintenance occurred, and a quality indicator for the passage operation. I excluded donor identity, conditioned-culture properties, the resulting serially passaged entity state, capture/instrument settings, raw signal files, and downstream genomic/phenotypic outputs because those belong to adjacent nodes. I also avoided repeating condition-setting fields from the earlier culture setup process. The selected fields are the minimum needed to reproduce the maintenance workflow and interpret passage-related effects on later genomic stability readouts.

md_schema.descr: Identifier for the passage-and-maintain protocol used under the assigned condition; use the study's maintenance protocol code if available (for example, PM01 or maintenance_A). Record once per maintenance workflow.

Interval between routine passages, measured in days from one split/transfer event to the next under the assigned condition. Typical iPSC maintenance intervals are about 2-7 days depending on growth rate.

Cell split ratio used at each routine passage, expressed as the ratio of starting culture to transferred fraction (for example, 1:6 or 1:10). Record the planned maintenance ratio for the passage workflow.
Method used to dissociate cells during passage and maintenance, describing whether cells were separated as clumps, single cells, or by another approach.
Volume of fresh maintenance medium added per passage or routine feed step, in milliliters, as used in the maintenance workflow. Record the value applied during the passage cycle.

Number of passage increments applied during this maintenance step relative to the prior culture state, usually 1 for a single routine passage but may be higher if multiple splits are grouped in one record.
Time spent performing the passage-and-maintain workflow for the culture event, in hours from start of dissociation/splitting to return to incubated maintenance conditions.

Overall operational quality assessment of the passage step, indicating whether the maintenance was performed as intended and whether any issues were noted that could affect later genomic stability interpretation.

serially_passaged_ipsc.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the culture state after repeated passage, so I included intrinsic passage-state descriptors that identify the passage level, culture age, expansion status, and readiness for downstream measurement. I excluded the maintenance protocol parameters from the upstream Process node, the assay configuration from downstream Capture nodes, and all raw/derived genomic or phenotype results. I also avoided duplicating donor, condition setup, or maintenance fields already defined upstream. The resulting fields describe the serially passaged culture itself, which is the biological material entering the measurement sessions.

md_schema.descr: Current passage number of the iPSC culture at the time this serially passaged entity was recorded; use the passage count used by the study (for example, P5 or P12) and store the numeric passage level as an integer.

Total number of days the culture had been maintained since the start of condition exposure or post-plating expansion when this passage-specific entity was captured. Record as days elapsed before downstream genomic stability measurements.
Estimated culture confluence at the time the serially passaged iPSC sample was prepared for measurement, expressed as percent surface coverage. Typical range is 0-100 percent.
General growth phase of the serially passaged culture immediately before measurement preparation, reflecting whether cells were in log-phase expansion, slowing growth, or near-confluence.
Approximate number of cells available from the serially passaged culture for downstream capture preparation, reported in millions of cells at the time of sampling.

Indication that the serially passaged culture met the study's readiness criteria for genomic stability assays, such as sufficient cell number, acceptable morphology, and absence of obvious contamination.
Batch or culture-run identifier assigned to the serially passaged culture preparation, used to distinguish replicate culture expansions within the same condition and passage level.

snp_array_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration descriptors for the SNP array assay: platform identity, scanner/model details, array design, configured run settings, and operator-controlled QC thresholds. I excluded sample provenance and passage-state properties from upstream Entity nodes, raw file properties from the downstream Signal node, and processed aberration calls from the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating the sequencing-related capture fields that belong to the separate WGS capture node. The selected fields are the minimum instrument and session descriptors needed to reproduce or interpret the SNP array acquisition.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the SNP array measurement session or run; use the study's capture-run code format (for example, SNP_RUN_01 or capture_A). Record one per array acquisition event.
Name of the SNP array platform used for capture, recorded at the time of measurement (for example, Illumina Infinium Global Screening Array or CytoSNP).
Hardware manufacturer of the SNP array scanner or capture system used for the measurement session; record the vendor of the actively configured instrument.
Model name or number of the SNP array instrument used for capture, recorded exactly as configured for the run (for example, iScan or equivalent).
Serial number of the SNP array instrument used for the capture session, recorded as a string in the manufacturer's format for traceability.
Manifest or probe annotation version used for the SNP array platform during capture, recorded as the reference design file version applied in the run.

Scanner resolution used for the SNP array acquisition, expressed in micrometers per pixel or scan setting units as configured for the run; typical values are platform-specific and should match the acquisition settings.
Duration of the array hybridization step associated with the capture session, measured in hours from sample loading to scan initiation. Record the actual configured hybridization time for the run.
Operator-defined quality-control threshold applied during SNP array capture, such as minimum signal intensity or call-rate criterion used to accept the run.

snp_array_raw_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only the raw data artifact properties: file naming/location, file format, size, dimensions, channel layout, and technical quality metrics that describe the acquired SNP array output. I excluded capture-session settings, instrument configuration, sample provenance, and downstream aberration calls because those belong to the Capture node, upstream Entity nodes, or the Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any assay-interpretation or QC thresholds already handled at capture. The fields below are the minimum raw-file descriptors needed for storage, retrieval, and technical assessment of the SNP array output.

md_schema.descr: Storage path or URI for the raw SNP array output file created by the measurement session; use a repository-relative path or accession-style URI (for example, s3://bucket/run01/sampleA.idat). Record at the signal level, not at capture.
File format of the raw SNP array data artifact, recorded as the exact technical format produced by the instrument or converter (for example, idat, txt, or vendor-specific binary format).
Size of the raw SNP array signal file in bytes, measured after acquisition and storage. Use this to support data integrity and transfer checks.
Number of probes represented in the raw SNP array data artifact, as captured in the signal file. Typical values are platform-specific and may range from tens of thousands to millions.
Number of measurement channels or color channels encoded in the raw SNP array signal file, as produced by the platform output.
Observed dynamic range of raw probe intensities in the signal artifact, recorded as the minimum-to-maximum usable intensity span or a comparable technical range summary at the raw-data stage.
Technical quality flag for the raw SNP array artifact, indicating whether the file passed basic integrity and signal-quality checks after acquisition.
Percent of SNP probes with successful genotype calls in the raw signal artifact, calculated as a technical data-quality metric for the acquired file. Typical values are 0-100 percent.

snp_calling.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational-processing details used to convert raw SNP array intensities into calls: software identity, version, repository, key algorithmic parameters, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded raw-file descriptors from the Signal node, the aberration table contents from the Derivative node, and all upstream capture/instrument settings because they are outside the computational transformation itself. I also avoided repeating sample identifiers or culture-state fields from earlier nodes. The selected fields are the minimum processing metadata needed to reproduce or audit the SNP calling step.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the SNP calling run or analysis job; use the study's processing-run code format (for example, SNP_CALL_01 or proc_A). Record one per computational conversion of raw array intensities.
Name of the software package or pipeline used to convert SNP array intensities into aberration calls and summarized copy-number results (for example, GenomeStudio or an equivalent calling tool).
Software version used for the SNP calling computation, recorded exactly as installed or executed in the processing environment.
Repository, package source, or distribution reference for the SNP calling software or pipeline, such as a vendor page, Git repository, or container source.
Algorithm or calling method used to infer copy-number changes from SNP array intensities, recorded as the specific model or heuristic applied during processing.
Whether loss-of-heterozygosity detection was enabled during the SNP calling step, indicating if the processing pipeline attempted to identify LOH events from the array data.
Minimum probe coverage or probe support threshold required for a genomic aberration to be called in the SNP processing step, expressed as the pipeline's configured cutoff value.
Overall quality status of the SNP calling process, indicating whether the computation completed successfully and met the study's processing acceptance criteria.

snp_aberration_calls.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result descriptors for the SNP aberration table: the output table identity, aberration content categories, key summary counts, genomic resolution, and result-level confidence/quality indicators. I excluded raw signal properties from the Signal node, computation parameters and software details from the Process node, and any capture/instrument settings or biological source metadata from upstream nodes. I also avoided overlapping with WGS-derived outputs. The selected fields are the minimum derived-result metadata needed to interpret, filter, and reuse the SNP-array aberration table.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived SNP aberration table produced from the calling step; use the study's result table code format (for example, SNP_ABN_01 or result_A). Record once per derived output table.
Total number of copy-number gain or loss events reported in the derived SNP aberration table for this sample or culture unit.
Total number of loss-of-heterozygosity events identified in the derived SNP aberration table for this sample or culture unit.

Approximate genomic resolution of copy-number aberration detection in the derived SNP result table, expressed in kilobases and reflecting the practical size threshold supported by the array and calling pipeline.
Types of aberrations represented in the derived table, summarizing which classes were called from the SNP data for this sample.
Overall confidence level assigned to the derived SNP aberration results, based on post-calling review or pipeline scoring of the table output.
Quality flag for the derived aberration table, indicating whether the result passed downstream acceptance checks and is suitable for integration with other outputs.

wgs_capture.reasoning: I corrected the WGS capture schema by removing field names that collided with previously generated DAG steps: capture_session_id, platform_name, instrument_manufacturer, instrument_model, and instrument_serial_number. To stay within the Capture node's semantic territory, I replaced them with WGS-specific acquisition fields that still describe the measurement session and instrument configuration without duplicating earlier metadata. I excluded raw signal, downstream processing, and biological source properties. The remaining fields capture WGS run identity, library/input settings, and operator-controlled acquisition parameters needed to document the sequencing session.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the whole-genome sequencing capture run; use the study's sequencing-run code format (for example, WGS_RUN_01 or wgs_capture_B). Record one per WGS acquisition event and do not reuse IDs from other assay capture steps.
Sequencing platform family used for the WGS capture session, recorded at acquisition time without repeating generic platform labels used elsewhere (for example, Illumina short-read sequencing).
Configured read length in base pairs for the WGS acquisition, measured at capture setup (for example, 150 bp paired-end reads).
Whether the WGS acquisition was configured as paired-end sequencing rather than single-end sequencing, recorded for the run setup.
Library preparation protocol used for the WGS capture session, recorded as the sequencing library workflow applied before loading onto the instrument.
Target sequencing depth in fold coverage configured for the WGS run, expressed as X-fold genome coverage (for example, 30x).
Operator- or pipeline-defined quality-control threshold applied to the WGS capture session, such as minimum cluster density, Q30 target, or yield cutoff used for acceptance.

Brief free-text note for any WGS acquisition-specific deviation, rerun condition, or batch note that affects interpretation of the sequencing session but is not represented by the structured fields above.

wgs_raw_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I kept only raw WGS artifact descriptors and replaced the colliding QC field with a distinct WGS-specific technical flag to avoid DAG-wide duplication. I excluded capture settings, biological provenance, and downstream processing/variant information because those belong to other node types. The fields below describe the raw file bundle itself and its technical properties, which are the appropriate semantic territory for this step.

md_schema.descr: Storage path or URI for the raw whole-genome sequencing data artifact generated by the capture session; use a repository-relative path or accession-style URI (for example, s3://bucket/run01/sampleA.fastq.gz). Record at the signal level, not at capture.
File format of the raw WGS data artifact, recorded as the exact technical format produced by the sequencing workflow (for example, fastq, fastq.gz, or bcl-converted read files).
Size of the raw WGS signal file or file bundle in bytes, measured after acquisition and storage. Use this for transfer and integrity checks.
Total number of sequencing reads contained in the raw WGS data artifact, counted at the signal stage before alignment or variant processing.
Total number of base pairs represented in the raw WGS signal artifact, recorded from the raw reads before downstream trimming or alignment.
Whether the raw WGS artifact contains paired-end read sets or single-end reads as stored in the signal file bundle.
Mean base-call quality score across the raw WGS reads, calculated as a technical quality metric directly from the signal artifact before alignment.
Technical integrity flag for the raw WGS artifact, indicating whether the file or read bundle passed basic storage, checksum, and read-level consistency checks after acquisition.

wgs_variant_processing.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result metadata for the WGS aberration output: result table identity, variant classes reported, counts of key variant types, structural-variant summary, genomic coordinate precision, and result-level confidence. I excluded raw reads, processing software parameters, capture/instrument configuration, and any upstream biological source fields because those belong to Signal, Process, Capture, or Entity nodes. I also avoided reusing any field names already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including shared generic QC labels. The fields below describe the final derived WGS aberration table itself, which downstream analysis will integrate with culture and phenotype data.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived WGS aberration table produced by the processing step; use the study's result code format (for example, WGS_ABN_01 or result_B). Record once per derived output table.
Classes of genomic changes represented in the derived WGS table for this sample, summarizing the types of variants or aberrations that were called.
Total number of single-nucleotide variants reported in the derived WGS aberration table for this sample or culture unit.
Total number of insertion and deletion events reported in the derived WGS aberration table for this sample or culture unit.
Total number of structural variants reported in the derived WGS aberration table for this sample or culture unit.
Approximate base-pair resolution at which the derived WGS results are reported, expressed as the effective coordinate precision used for variant localization.
Overall confidence score assigned to the derived WGS aberration results, based on post-processing filtering or caller support for the reported events.
Estimated sensitivity of the WGS calling pipeline for detecting true variants at the configured depth and filtering regime, expressed as a study-defined fraction or percentage if reported.

wgs_aberration_calls.reasoning: For this WGS-derived step, I avoided all previously colliding generic result-table and summary fields already used elsewhere in the DAG. I kept the schema narrowly focused on additional derivative metadata that characterizes the WGS aberration calls without duplicating earlier output identifiers or summary metrics: event-type-specific filters, copy-number/allele-balance summaries, structural-variant breakpoint support, and pathogenicity/annotation summaries. I excluded raw reads, processing details, capture settings, and any fields already generated under prior WGS or SNP derivative nodes. The selected fields help downstream users interpret the content and filtering of this specific derived WGS aberration set while respecting DAG-wide uniqueness.

md_schema.descr: Name or short description of the post-calling filter set applied to the WGS aberration calls before they were accepted into the derived table; record the study's filter label or version string (for example, strict_filters_v2).

Minimum variant allele fraction required for an event to appear in the derived WGS aberration table, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1. Record the threshold used by the final calling and filtering stage.
Summary of copy-number state categories represented in the derived WGS call set for this sample, describing whether gains, losses, neutral states, or complex changes were present.
Number of structural-variant breakpoint pairs or breakpoint-supported events retained in the derived WGS result after filtering; this captures structural call support rather than total reads.
Count of variants in the derived WGS aberration set that were annotated as pathogenic or likely pathogenic by the study's annotation rules or reference database.
Reference annotation database or knowledge base used to label variants in the derived WGS aberration table (for example, ClinVar, COSMIC, or an internal database).
Short narrative note summarizing notable features of the derived WGS aberration set, such as an unusually high burden, clustered events, or absence of large-scale abnormalities.

phenotype_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the observation-session and measurement-configuration descriptors for phenotype assessment: who performed it, when, what microscopy/observation setup was used, and the operator-controlled criteria for scoring morphology and growth-related changes. I excluded donor and culture provenance from upstream Entity nodes, any derived phenotype labels from the downstream Derivative node, and all genomic assay fields from the SNP/WGS branches. I also avoided repeating any previously generated generic capture identifiers or instrument fields that have already collided elsewhere in the DAG. The fields below describe the active phenotype observation session only, which is the appropriate scope for a Capture node.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the phenotype observation session or inspection event; use the study's capture code format for phenotype assessment (for example, PHENO_RUN_01 or capture_C). Record once per observation session.

Method used to observe culture phenotype during the capture session, such as brightfield microscopy, phase-contrast microscopy, or visual inspection. Record the actual configured observation approach.
Manufacturer of the microscope or imaging system used for phenotype capture, recorded as the actively configured hardware vendor.
Model name or number of the microscope or imaging system used for phenotype capture, recorded exactly as configured for the observation session.
Serial number of the microscope or imaging system used for phenotype capture, recorded in the manufacturer's traceability format.
Objective or total magnification used during phenotype observation, expressed as an x-fold magnification setting (for example, 10x or 20x).
Time point of the phenotype observation relative to the relevant culture event, measured in hours from the start of the condition or the most recent passage.
Operator-defined criteria used during the capture session to assess morphology and growth-related phenotype changes, such as colony compactness, differentiation, or abnormal growth behavior.
Quality flag for the phenotype observation session, indicating whether the capture produced usable observations and met basic assessment criteria.

phenotype_derivative.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed/recorded phenotype outputs derived from the capture session: a phenotype record identifier, the observed phenotype categories, summary severity, whether the change was growth- or morphology-related, and confidence/status fields. I excluded the observation-session setup and microscope configuration from the Capture node, as well as any culture-protocol, genomic, or upstream entity metadata. I also avoided reusing any previously generated generic result identifiers or QC flags that have already collided elsewhere in the DAG. The selected fields describe the derived phenotype record itself, which is the appropriate output of this node.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived phenotype record produced from the observation session; use the study's result code format (for example, PHENO_RES_01 or result_C). Record once per derived phenotype output.
Primary category of phenotype observed in the derived record, describing the broad type of morphology or growth change linked to the cultured iPSC line.
Overall severity of the derived phenotype observation, summarizing how pronounced the morphology or growth change was in the recorded culture.
Numeric score summarizing the derived phenotype observation from the capture session, where higher values indicate stronger or more pronounced abnormality or deviation from expected iPSC appearance.
Relative growth rate of the observed culture compared with the matched control or reference culture, expressed as a ratio or fold-change summarized in the derived record.
Confidence assigned to the derived phenotype record based on observation consistency, image quality, and operator agreement when applicable.
Brief description of the rule or summarization approach used to convert the observation session into the derived phenotype record, such as manual scoring or standardized rubric aggregation.

integrated_stability_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the integration workflow details: analysis software, version, repository, integration strategy, comparison design, and a process-level output quality indicator. I excluded upstream genomic and phenotype result content, culture protocol raw details, and downstream final table fields because those belong to the input Derivative/Entity nodes or the output Derivative node. I also avoided duplicating any identifiers or QC/status fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG by using integration-specific names. The fields below are the minimum metadata needed to reproduce or audit the stability-analysis step that combines all upstream evidence.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated stability analysis job or run; use the study's analysis-run code format (for example, STAB_01 or analysis_A). Record one per integration workflow execution.
Name of the software package or pipeline used to integrate genomic aberration calls, phenotype records, and culture protocol details (for example, R, Python, or a custom analysis workflow).
Software version used for the integrated stability analysis, recorded exactly as installed or executed in the analysis environment.
Repository, package source, or workflow reference for the integrated stability-analysis code, such as a Git repository, package release, or container source.
Method used to combine genomic, phenotype, and culture metadata in the stability analysis, such as table join, mixed-model analysis, weighted scoring, or rule-based integration.
Comparison scheme used in the analysis to evaluate how culture conditions affect stability, such as against a matched control, across oxygen levels, or across media supplement groups.
Statistical correction method applied during the integrated analysis when multiple conditions or aberration tests were evaluated, such as FDR or Bonferroni correction.
Overall quality indicator for the integrated stability-analysis run, reflecting whether the combined analysis completed successfully and produced interpretable output.

stability_metadata_table.reasoning: This is the final Derivative node, so I included only fields that describe the integrated output table itself: table identity, row/granularity, linked upstream source set, integrated stability summary, condition-effect summary, and output quality. I excluded all detailed culture, donor, passage, genomic, and phenotype contents because those already belong to upstream nodes and would duplicate their territory. I also avoided repeating any field names already generated elsewhere in the DAG by using output-table-specific identifiers rather than generic QC or result labels. The fields below provide the minimum metadata needed for a downstream user to understand and reuse the final integrated stability metadata table.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final integrated stability metadata table; use the study's table code format (for example, STAB_TBL_01 or table_A). Record once per final output table.
Unit represented by each row in the integrated table, such as one donor-line-condition-passage combination or one sample-level summary. Record the intended analysis granularity of the final table.

Summary of the upstream data types incorporated into the final table, indicating whether donor context, culture protocol details, passage information, genomic aberration results, and phenotype observations were all included in the integration.

High-level stability interpretation assigned in the final table, summarizing whether the culture condition is associated with preserved genomic integrity, moderate instability, or pronounced instability.

Direction of the inferred culture-condition effect on genomic stability in the final integrated table, capturing whether the condition appears protective, neutral, or destabilizing relative to the comparison framework used in the analysis.
Number of rows contained in the integrated stability metadata table at the time of release, used to document output size and completeness.
Storage or exchange format of the integrated stability table, recorded as the technical output format used for downstream reuse (for example, csv, tsv, parquet, or xlsx).
Release status of the final integrated table, indicating whether it is a preliminary draft, internally reviewed version, or final approved output for downstream interpretation.
